content.comment_body: Hello, When building a user-defined function (UDF) block, I noticed that inputs and outputs could sometimes be connected directly. However, I received an error stating "Incompatible connectors." This issue has occurred before: attempting a direct I-Q connection often fails, but retrying sometimes works. My question is whether directly connecting I-Q is considered normal practice or should be avoided?

Hi, Certain blocks are not permitted within a UDF, including I and Q. Essentially, a UDF operates similarly to other special functions; I and Q must be connected only at the block's inputs and outputs and are not allowed within a UDF itself. Additionally, you cannot include message text within a UDF. If you attempt to use restricted blocks when creating a UDF from existing code, the system delivers a clear warning message. I hope this clarifies things.
Hi, Thank you for the information, [user_name]!

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain about how to correctly connect I and Q connectors within user-defined function blocks. An error about incompatible connectors reveals unclear product guidance regarding permitted connections, particularly since I and Q are not allowed inside UDFs but can be linked at the boundaries. Insufficient documentation and ambiguous error feedback create confusion and may disrupt workflow.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect either the ability to directly connect I and Q connectors within UDF blocks or to receive explicit instructions explaining why such connections are restricted.
